extracted.intended_audience: Users of the Singular/Plural computer algebra system (researchers and practitioners in computational/non-commutative algebra)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for the non-commutative subsystem of the Singular/Plural computer algebra system, listing commands (syntax, types, purpose), usage notes, limitations, and examples for each routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: eliminate (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: eliminate(ideal_expression, product_of_ring_variables) / eliminate(module_expression, product_of_ring_variables) — eliminates variables occurring as factors of the second argument from an ideal (resp. submodule) by intersecting it with the subring that does not contain these variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: same as first argument. eliminate neither needs a special ordering on the basering nor a Groebner basis as input. Does not work in non-commutative quotients. In a non-commutative algebra, not every subset of variables generates a proper subalgebra; if the subalgebra is not admissible no elimination is possible and an error is reported. Example shows eliminating parameter 'a' succeeds, but trying to eliminate 'h' fails because the subalgebra generated by e,f is not closed (f*e - e*f = -h).

rubrics_metrics.name: envelope
rubrics_metrics.description: envelope(ring_name) — creates an enveloping algebra Aenv = A ⊗_K Aopp (opposite algebra).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: ring. Purpose: creates the enveloping algebra of a given algebra. You must activate the returned ring with setring. See explanation of opposite. Example: for U(sl_2) this doubles variables (creates 6 vars) and sets noncommutative relations accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: fetch (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: fetch(ring_name, name) — maps objects between rings using positional mapping (i-th variable of source maps to i-th variable of basering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: number, poly, vector, ideal, module, matrix or list (same as second arg). Purpose: convenient to change variable names/orderings or to map objects from a ring to a quotient ring and vice versa. Compared with imap, fetch uses positions not names. Coefficient fields must be compatible. Example: fetching Groebner basis generators from Usl2 into a factor-algebra and standardizing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: imap (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: imap(ring_name, name) — identity map on common subrings using names: maps variables/parameters of the same name identically, others to 0; can map parameters to variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: numbers, polynomials, vectors, ideals, modules, matrices or lists. Purpose: mapping between rings/qrings with compatible ground fields; useful for mappings from homogenized rings to original rings or between rings with/without parameters. Compared with fetch, imap uses names not positions. Example: mapping ideals to a parameter ring and computing central-character ideals; then performing imap to bring them into another ring and std to get characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: intersect (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: intersect(expression_list_of_ideal_expressions) / intersect(expression_list_of_module_expressions) — computes intersection of ideals or modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: ideal or module. Purpose: compute intersections. Examples: intersections in anti-commutative algebra and in Weyl algebra; outputs can be nontrivial polynomials (examples shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: kbase (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: kbase(ideal_or_module_expression [, int]) — computes vector space basis of factor-module (ring/free module modulo ideal/submodule generated by initial terms of given generators); with degree argument returns part of basis of given monomial degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: same as input. Purpose: with one argument returns basis of quotient defined by leading terms; if quotient not finite dimensional returns -1. If generators form a Groebner basis this is the vector space basis of the factor-module. In non-commutative case, ring modulo ideal has ring structure iff ideal is two-sided; kbase respects module-grading given by isHomog attribute. Examples: U(sl_2) quotient with kbase returning basis elements and vdim showing dimension 4; usage with degree argument to get monomials of a specific degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: lift (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: lift(ideal_expression, subideal_expression) / lift(module_expression, submodule_expression) — computes the (left) transformation matrix expressing generators of a submodule in terms of generators of a module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: matrix. Purpose: compute transformation matrix T with transpose(T)*transpose(matrix(m)) = transpose(matrix(sm)) (more precise linear algebra description in manual). Uses different algorithms depending whether modules are given by Groebner bases. Gives a warning if sm is not a submodule. Example: compute lift for parametric U(sl_2) ideal to get matrix T and verify ideal equality via transpose(T)*transpose(matrix(i)). See also liftstd.

rubrics_metrics.name: liftstd (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: liftstd(ideal_or_module_expression, matrix_name [, module_name]) — returns a left Groebner basis of an ideal/module and a left transformation matrix from the given ideal/module to that Groebner basis; optional third argument returns left syzygy module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: ideal or module. Purpose: compute left Groebner basis and transformation matrix T; if third arg provided, also return left syzygy module. Example: for U(sl_2) returns Groebner basis j and matrix T; verifying that ideal(transpose(T)*transpose(matrix(i))) equals j and computing syzygies S when requested. See lift for relation between T, m and sm.

rubrics_metrics.name: minres (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: minres(list_expression) / minres(resolution_expression) — minimizes a free resolution of an ideal or module given by the list or resolution expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: list or resolution. Purpose: minimize free resolution (removes redundant summands from second module on). Example: generate a resolution with nres/mres then call minres to produce a minimized resolution; betti numbers can be printed before/after. Note: resolution not minimized until minres applied; examples show changes in betti table.

rubrics_metrics.name: modulo (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: modulo(ideal_expression, ideal_expression) or modulo(module_expression, module_expression) — represents h1/(h1 ∩ h2) ≅ (h1 + h2)/h2 and returns generators of the kernel of the induced map; for ideals/modules inside same free module R^l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: module. Purpose: compute kernel of induced map H1 : R^k → R^l/Im(H2). Returns generators of kernel; sets isHomog attribute when appropriate. Example: compute modulo(H1,H2) for U(sl_2) ideals and derive generators; see also syz.

rubrics_metrics.name: mres (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: mres(ideal_or_module_expression, int) — computes a minimal free resolution of an ideal or module with the Groebner basis method; stops after k steps if int k is nonzero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: resolution. Purpose: compute free resolution of coker(A) where A is matrix(M). mres(M,0) returns a resolution with at most n+2 modules where n is number of variables. List L = mres(M,0) has L[1] minimal generators of M, L[2] minimal generators of first syzygy module, etc. Accessing single elements may trigger partial computations; assigning whole list recommended. Examples show creating mres for ideal i in U(sl_2) and verifying exactness via size(ideal(transpose(l[2])*transpose(l[1]))). See minres for minimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: nc_algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: nc_algebra(C, D) or nc_algebra(n, D) or nc_algebra(C, p) or nc_algebra(n, p) — in basering r (k variables) creates non-commutative extension of r subject to relations x_j x_i = c_{ij} x_i x_j + d_{ij} for i<j, where C (upper triangular) holds c_{ij} and D holds polynomial d_{ij}. If all c_{ij}=n you may pass number n; if all d_{ij}=p you may pass polynomial p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: ring. Purpose: construct G-algebras/non-commutative algebras with specified structural coefficients/polynomials. Returned ring should be setring'd. Remark: Plural does not check non-degeneracy conditions for G-algebras when setting an algebra. Examples: quantum deformation U'_q(so_3), U(sl_3), quasi-commutative algebra, algebra with n=-1 and polynomial p=3w. See Section 7.4.1 for G-algebra details. Use ncalg.lib/nctools.lib for helpers.

rubrics_metrics.name: ncalgebra (deprecated)
rubrics_metrics.description: ncalgebra(...) — works like nc_algebra but changes the basering; deprecated and should be replaced by nc_algebra followed by setring and explicit mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: none. Purpose/Remark: ncalgebra violates general policy of changing basering; replace with def A = nc_algebra(C,D); setring A; then map objects as needed. See nc_algebra for behavior; ncalgebra maintained for compatibility only.

rubrics_metrics.name: nres (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: nres(ideal_or_module_expression, int) — computes a free resolution of an ideal or module which is minimized from the second module on (via Groebner basis method).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: resolution. Purpose: compute free resolution where second and later modules are minimized; resolution may still be further minimized by minres. Use betti to compute Betti numbers. Example: nres(i,0) on ideal i in U(sl_2) produces resolution; verifying exactness and printing betti before/after minres illustrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: oppose
rubrics_metrics.description: oppose(ring_name, name) — for a given object in a given ring, creates its opposite object in the opposite ring (current ring assumed to be the opposite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: poly, vector, ideal, module or matrix (same as second arg). Purpose: construct opposite object; (Oopp)opp = O. Example: oppose applied to poly, vector, ideal, matrix, module and printing checks against imap show zero difference. See also envelope and opposite.

rubrics_metrics.name: opposite
rubrics_metrics.description: opposite(ring_name) — creates an opposite algebra of a given algebra (same vector space but multiplication reversed: f * g := g·f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: ring. Purpose: produce opposite algebra; activate with setring. Opposite algebra reorders variables (x1..xN becomes XN..X1) and uses an opposed ordering (<_opp) given by reversing columns of matrix ordering. Not implemented for non-global orderings currently. Example: create opposite of quantum deformation algebra and verify (B-opp)-opp = B.

rubrics_metrics.name: preimage (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: preimage(ring_name, map_name, ideal_name) or preimage(ring_name, ideal_expression, ideal_name) — returns preimage of an ideal under a given map (map from basering to given ring), i.e., computes preimage ideal in source ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: ideal. Purpose: compute preimage; to compute kernel of a map determine preimage of zero. Remark: in non-commutative case implemented only for maps A -> B where A is commutative. Example: mapping parameter 'a' to central element C in U(sl_2) and preimage yields central characters factorized giving simple characters; preimage of zero yields kernel.

rubrics_metrics.name: quotient (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: quotient(ideal_expression, ideal_expression) or quotient(module_expression, module_expression) or quotient(module_expression, ideal_expression) — computes ideal quotient {a ∈ R | aJ ⊂ I} or module quotient {b ∈ R^n | bJ ⊂ M}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: ideal (for ideal-ideal) or module (for module-ideal). Purpose: compute ideal/module quotients. Note: can only be used for two-sided ideals (bimodules), otherwise result may have no meaning. Examples: quotient in quantum plane and quotient(I,H) for U(sl_2) producing compact presentations of Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: reduce (plural) / NF
rubrics_metrics.description: reduce(poly_or_vector_or_ideal_or_module, ideal_or_module [, int]) — reduces to left normal form with respect to an ideal/module represented by left Groebner basis; NF is synonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: same as first argument. Purpose: returns 0 iff first arg is element (resp. subideal/submodule) of second arg (when second is left Groebner basis). Optional third int argument 1 forces reduction considering only leading term (no tail reduction). Example: compute central characters via reduce(z,I), use NF to produce member of J, test membership by reduce(...,J) returning 0. reduce(I,J) example returns several entries showing how generators reduce. See std and twostd interplays.

rubrics_metrics.name: ringlist (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: ringlist(ring_or_qring) — decomposes a ring/qring into a list of components describing the ring structure: base field, coefficient field, variable names, orderings, and in non-commutative case two extra matrices (C and D) giving G-algebra structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: list. Purpose: decompose ring into components (first 4 components common, 5th and 6th for non-commutative: upper triangular matrix C with structural coefficients and square matrix D with structural polynomials corresponding to G-algebra C and D). After modification, one can construct ring(list). Example: use ringlist on quantized Weyl algebra, edit matrices l[5], l[6] to change relation and reconstruct ring. Useful for programmatic ring modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: slimgb (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: slimgb(ideal_or_module) — returns a left Groebner basis of a left ideal or module with respect to the global monomial ordering, using algorithms aiming to keep polynomials/vectors slim (short with small coefficients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type: same as argument. Purpose: compute Groebner basis optimized for keeping expressions slim; designed by Michael Brickenstein. Notes: currently best results over function fields (parameters); may not be optimal for weighted degree orderings. Supports options prot (protocol output) and redSB (return reduced Groebner basis). Protocol messages: M[n,m] for parallel reduction, b for exchange trick, e adds a reductor with non-minimal leading term. Works for graded commutative algebras but not general GR-algebras (use qslimgb instead). Examples compare slimgb with std showing equality of Groebner bases for U(sl_2) example; also example for exterior algebras.
